subject: System Design
title: In-Memory Databases
description: A short lesson to help you apply In-Memory Databases.

hook.text: Redis responds in under 1 millisecond. How? It keeps all data in RAM, not on disk.

buildup.text: RAM is 1,000x faster than SSD. In-memory databases trade durability for extreme speed.

discovery.text: Redis, Memcached, and VoltDB all live in memory. They're used for caching, sessions, and leaderboards.

twist.text: RAM is volatile — a crash erases everything. In-memory databases use snapshots and logs for persistence.

climax.text: In-memory databases aren't a replacement for disk databases — they complement them for speed-critical paths.

punchline.text: Keep hot data in memory for sub-millisecond access.

quiz.question: Why are in-memory databases so fast?
options: They keep all data in RAM which is 1,000x faster than SSD
